Rotherham vs Crewe is the standout statistical curiosity — Crewe have drawn their last five in a row and Rotherham draw constantly at home, making the X arguably the clearest single outcome on the card. predictions.analysis: This is the flagship League A Nations League opener at Wembley, and by any reasonable measure it is Spain who arrive as clear favourites. The world champions come equipped with arguably their finest generation — Pedri, Rodri, Zubimendi and Lamine Yamal headlining a squad that blends technical mastery with relentless pressing. Thomas Tuchel faces a baptism of fire in only his second competitive camp, and the absences reportedly plaguing his squad make the task considerably harder. All injury information here is sourced from Perplexity previews and must be treated as reportedly out, unverified by structured data — but if even half the named five absentees (Declan Rice, Cole Palmer, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento) are confirmed, England are missing their spine. Rice in particular is irreplaceable as the defensive anchor; Palmer and Mainoo gave England their Euro 2024 attacking cutting edge. Spain's absences — goalkeeper Joan García, right-back Pedro Porro, and suspended Gavi — are meaningful but far less damaging. Luis de la Fuente can call upon Unai Simón in goal and rotate wide without losing tactical identity. The tactical picture is straightforward: Spain will dominate possession through midfield overloads, expose England's makeshift midfield, and create through Yamal's runs. England will need to be disciplined and dangerous on the counter. The odds at Spain 2.55 are competitive but fair given the circumstances. The market's 47% public backing for Spain aligns with the analytical verdict. A home draw is always possible at Wembley given emotional crowd support and England's defensive resolve under Tuchel's early imprint, but Spain's quality differential is simply too pronounced — especially against a depleted English unit.
predictions.value_note: Spain at 2.55 is borderline value given the reported injury crisis for England — if absences are confirmed, Spain are arguably worth 2.10 or shorter.

Rotherham's home record mirrors this tendency: D-W-D in their last three at the New York Stadium, and their overall form of W-D-L-D-W confirms they share points frequently.
